title: lexio: Generalized Input-Output Model with Preemptive Goal Programming
description:
An R package for input-output models solved by preemptive (lexicographic) goal programming. The user declares an input-output database: the technical structure (Z, A or B = I - A), gross output x, final demand f, any number of satellite accounts (levels E or coefficients D, as vectors in R or as CSV/.xlsx files) and, optionally, a corridor that bounds the deviations of the economic goals on both sides, only below or only above, as a proportion of each goal. The user also declares the direction (>=, <= or =) and the goal of each account, the scenarios and the priorities. Sectoral output is chosen to meet the goals in priority order, written as G x + d- - d+ = g with G = [D; I - A]. Each priority level is a linear program solved with GLPK, with the optima of the earlier levels locked. By default the package runs all k! orders of the k satellite accounts, with the economic block fixed at the last level; the operator may list the orderings to run, with several weighted goals per level, move the economic block only by an explicit declaration, and choose absolute or relative economic deviations. Runs where GLPK reports a numerical false infeasibility are solved again with a slightly relaxed lock and flagged. Every level of every run is written to a report, CSV tables and an Excel workbook.

Documentation: the vignettes of the package (getting started, declaring data and models, the goal programming example of Miller and Blair, and the replication of the thesis), with Portuguese translations on the website https://filipevascrocha.github.io/lexio/.

The folder replication/ reproduces the results of the doctoral thesis that introduced the model (Rocha, 2026, PPGE/UFJF), on the Brazilian fuel and electricity markets with the 2018 input-output matrix with energy-sector detail published by EPE (Empresa de Pesquisa Energética) in partnership with FIPE. The declared database of the thesis is the file lexio-thesis-data-2018.zip, attached to the GitHub release v1.0.0 at https://github.com/FilipeVascRocha/lexio/releases/tag/v1.0.0. It also holds a dictionary of every file and column and the EPE workbook itself, unchanged, so that the database can be rebuilt even if the workbook leaves the EPE site; replication/01_declare_data.R builds the database from that workbook.
